**In one line**: OpenAI reportedly told lawmakers in a letter that it is developing "automated shutdown" capabilities for its AI tools.

### Key points
- According to a report by India's The Hindu, OpenAI is said to have described "automated shutdown" capabilities for AI tools in a letter to lawmakers.
- An automated shutdown is understood to act as a safeguard that halts an AI system when it behaves unexpectedly or when risk signals are detected.
- The letter was reportedly submitted to legislators amid ongoing policy discussions around AI regulation and safety.

### Why it matters
It signals AI companies moving to explain their safety controls directly to regulators. "Kill switch"–style controls are a central issue in AI-regulation debates worldwide, so how such a mechanism is actually implemented could shape future policy standards.
